Current main plan

Open B2-1 feedback-only repairs and the independent B2-2 → fresh-evaluation table.

The existing S_A2 and S_B2 results below used source/tests and are supplementary. They cannot be relabeled as B2-1. The README repair and fresh B2 sections are the retained B2-2 branch.

Retained native and supplementary source endpoints

A1 is an independent control. A2 failures feed two separate branches: source-only snippet recovery, and source-informed README repair. Fresh B2 follows README repair. Post-B2 source recovery is an additional endpoint.

B1 · Historical original-documentation repair arm: excluded from the revised study at the user’s request. It is not a pending run or a zero score. S_A2 is the independent source-only recovery branch from A2, not a renamed historical B1 result.

Exact native test counts

“Other recorded failures” includes execution, compilation, input and dependency failures; it does not certify that the target API was reached. Provider-unresolved rows are separate.

Two test layers around the repaired README

1. README repair-time validation

Source/tests deep dive → diagnosis → rewrite one entry → zero-fix validation. Up to five document rounds, with the configured stuck threshold of two.

These tests guide which edits are retained. They are part of the repair process.

2. B2 · Fresh full-manifest evaluation

After the repaired README is frozen, a fresh reader produces new snippets for the full manifest. Zero snippet fixes.

This is the fresh run on the README updated using the source deep dive. It does not inherit the validation snippets or S_A2 repairs.

Retained document loop and supplementary post-B2 loop · not the new B2-1 arm

These are two testing layers, not two independent B2 treatment arms. S_B2 then repairs remaining snippets using source/tests while keeping the B2 README unchanged. There is no separately updated README or additional fresh-README experiment after S_B2 in this protocol.

Why the net improvement can look small

Gross recoveries and new failures are different groups. A pass can mean normal API use, an exception-contract check, or only a skipped branch. Native scores below remain unchanged.
